transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2027-08-04
Time: 16:00 - 16:45 PT
Duration: ~45 minutes
Attendees: Liam O'Connor (Redwood AE), Priya Menon (Redwood CSM), Diego Ruiz (Redwood SE); Marta Lopez (Springwell Head of MLOps), Ethan Cole (CTO), Samira Khan (PM)

[00:00] Liam (Redwood): Hey everyone, thanks for joining, super excited to kick off. quick intro round?
[00:12] Marta (Springwell): hi yes Marta here, head of m-l-ohps, sorry m-lops, I run the models and infra for clinical triage.
[00:18] Ethan (Springwell): Ethan, CTO, focusing on infra and compliance.
[00:22] Samira (Springwell): Samira, product, I'll be managing the pilot and success criteria.
[00:30] Liam: Great, on our side Priya is our customer success lead, Diego is the se who will help with infra & benchmarks.
[00:38] Priya (Redwood): hey all, I'll coordinate onboarding and check-ins.
[00:42] Diego (Redwood): hi, will jump into the tech details shortly.

[01:15] Liam: quick agenda: roles, current stack, security checklist, pilot scope and timeline, then action items. sound good?
[01:25] Marta: yep good.

[02:10] Ethan: high level on infra: we run kubernetes on-prem for PHI-adjacent workloads, we have a private VPC in Azure for other services. our concerns are data residency and ensuring we don't send PHI outside our network.
[02:28] Diego: got it. Redwood supports private deployments and we also have Dedicated capacity. for pilot are you thinking hosted API or dedicated GPUs?
[02:40] Marta: ideally we want to try hosted for speed of integration, but if PHI is in requests we need private deployment or ensure de-identification upstream.
[02:52] Samira: our first use case is patient message triage, messages will be stripped of names by our preprocessor but may include sensitive clinical terms. latency requirement is sub 800ms p95 for typical queries, ideally under 500ms for short prompts.

[03:30] Diego: quick note: p95 latency depends on model choice and batching. we can propose a quantized smaller model on Dedicated for lower cost with predictable latency. hosted can be fast but noisy during peak.
[03:50] Ethan: what's the easiest path to get us running without opening our network? we want minimal uplift to ops.
[04:05] Priya: two options: 1) Redwood hosted API with strict pre-processing and no PHI sent; 2) Redwood Private (VPC / on-prem) where the control plane is customer-managed. for pilot many customers start hosted with de-id and then evaluate Dedicated/private for production.

[05:20] Marta: can you share SOC2 docs and SSO flow? we require SAML SSO, audit logs and KMS for keys.
[05:30] Liam: yes, we'll share SOC2 and our security packet; SAML is supported, we support IDP initiated and SP initiated flows. KMS: we integrate with customer KMS or we can host keys depending on deployment.
[05:45] Ethan: does Redwood support customer-managed CMKs in Azure?
[05:50] Diego: yes, we integrate with common KMS providers; for Private we can tie into your Azure Key Vault or customer HSM for encryption at rest.

[07:00] Samira: pilot success criteria: 1) p95 latency <800ms for the triage prompts, 2) run 10k messages/day with cost under $X per 1k (we'll share target), 3) no PHI leakage and audit logs available.
[07:25] Liam: good, we'll map those to measurable metrics and propose a pilot SLA.

[08:10] Diego: about instrumentation: we can enable Redwood Console dashboards for per-route latency, token costs, and request traces. you can also get token-level cost breakdowns.
[08:30] Marta: great — how hard is it to integrate our existing logging?
[08:35] Diego: we expose tracing hooks and can forward logs to your logging endpoint; for private setups you can keep logs internal.

[09:40] Ethan: what about model pinning and rollouts? we want deterministic behavior during pilot.
[09:47] Liam: Redwood supports model pinning and can do canary rollouts. we'll lock to a model version for the pilot and set automatic fallback to a smaller model if latency spikes.

[11:05] Samira: timeline — we want pilot running in two weeks and a production decision in 6 weeks. is that realistic?
[11:13] Priya: two weeks for a minimal pilot is aggressive but doable if we get prompts and a staging account quickly. Diego can provision staging and run smoke tests.
[11:25] Diego: yes if you share sample prompts and traffic shape we can set up a pipeline and baseline benchmarks within 5-7 business days.

[12:20] Marta: sample prompts we can share this afternoon — mostly short triage messages ~20-60 tokens.
[12:30] Liam: perfect. also any compliance questionnaires?
[12:35] Ethan: we have a vendor security questionnaire we'll send, plus specific data residency questions.

[13:50] Diego: quick tech nit: we have optimizations like KV cache and prefix caching which help for conversational workloads — might not be big win for single-turn triage, but batching and quantization will lower cost.
[14:10] Marta: you mentioned KV cache — is that safe for PII?
[14:20] Diego: cache is controlled by configuration; for sensitive data we recommend disabling persistent caching or storing caches in customer-managed storage inside your VPC.

[16:00] Liam: any blockers from your side?
[16:05] Marta: legal needs SOC2 and data processing addendum (DPA); procurement will review pricing.
[16:12] Priya: we'll include DPA template with the security packet.

[17:40] Samira: for cost estimates can you provide both hosted and dedicated equivalents for our expected volume?
[17:50] Diego: yes we'll run a cost model. need your expected token counts per message and messages/day.

[19:00] Marta: one more: can we run an on-prem variant for production if needed?
[19:06] Liam: yes, Redwood Private and on-prem packaging exists — we'll map the differences and operational overhead in the doc we send.

[21:30] Ethan: how do you handle audit logs and retention?
[21:36] Diego: audit logs can be forwarded to your SIEM or stored in customer-controlled buckets; retention is configurable per contract; for Dedicated we can provide longer retention as an add-on.

[24:00] Priya: recapping next steps: Redwood will send SOC2 + SAML checklist + DPA template; Diego will provision staging account and run baseline bench; Springwell to share prompts and traffic profile; schedule infra deep-dive.
[24:20] Marta: that sounds right.

[26:00] Liam: any competitors or existing vendors in play we should know?
[26:05] Ethan: we're talking to OpenAI and Vertex AI teams, and evaluating Anthropic for safety features.
[26:15] Liam: good to know — we'll highlight Redwood's Dedicated predictability and Private options in the packet.

[28:30] Diego: quick note on data flow diagrams — we'd like your network diagram to plan VPC peering or private endpoints.
[28:40] Ethan: will share by EOD.

[32:00] Samira: approvals — who needs to be in the weekly check-ins?
[32:05] Marta: I'll own from MLOps, Ethan for infra, Samira for product. We'll add a security reviewer from legal for the kick-off DPA review.

[36:10] Priya: we'll set up a recurring weekly 30 min check-in starting next Tuesday.

[38:40] Liam: any final Qs?
[38:45] Marta: none from me.
[38:48] Ethan: no.
[38:50] Samira: nope.

[39:00] Liam: ok thanks everyone — we'll follow up with the packet and staging creds.
[39:10] Priya: action items and calendar invite for weekly check-ins coming after the call.
[39:18] Diego: I'll start provisioning once I get the list of sample prompts.

[39:30] Meeting end / polite goodbyes

Notes about transcript quality: some terms auto-transcribed (K V cache -> K V cash), minor speaker label swaps in a few lines.
